facts.raw_span: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
afebrile
blood pressure was 110/80 mmHg
firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
carcinoembryonic antigen 1.14 ng/mL
CA-125 21 U/mL
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor
double inferior vena cava was identified, with the left cava draining via the left renal vein to the right-sided cava

support_spans: Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a bulky uterus with multiple fibroids
concepts.why: The ultrasound and CT findings confirm the presence of multiple uterine fibroids.

support_spans: lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
concepts.why: The patient's lifelong history of non-pitting edema suggests a diagnosis of lymphedema.

concepts.why: The CT findings confirm the presence of a double inferior vena cava, an anatomical variation.

rationales.F01: Right lower abdominal pain is a common symptom of ovarian tumors.
rationales.F02: Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora is a characteristic feature of lymphedema.
rationales.F05: A firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant is suggestive of an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F06: A right adnexal mass confirmed by bimanual pelvic examination is indicative of an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F09: Multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa are consistent with uterine fibroids and an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F10: A well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion in the abdominopelvic region is highly suggestive of an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F11: A provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor is based on the imaging findings and clinical presentation.
rationales.F12: A double inferior vena cava is a rare anatomical variation that is not directly related to the other conditions.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of a firm, non-tender, mobile mass and imaging findings of a large hypoechoic lesion and a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion in the right adnexa decided it
